Golem

Golem is a three-to-six player, five-card poker game using a 52-card deck. It requires a Dealer and begins with the amulet at the player to the Dealer’s right. The module tracks antes, betting, discards, the golem hand, pot carry-over, and the house share.

Deal and betting

Every participant antes. The Dealer deals five cards to each player. Starting with the amulet holder, participants may bet, match, raise, or fold until all remaining players have matched or folded.

Draw

Each remaining player may discard up to two cards and receives replacements. Every discard enters the face-down central discard pile. A second betting round begins with the amulet holder.

Showdown

If only one player remains, that player wins the pot less the house’s 5% share. Otherwise, each remaining player reveals their hand and the Dealer reveals the golem hand: the best five-card poker hand from the discard pile. The best player hand must strictly beat the golem hand to win. If it fails, that player adds twice the ante to the pot and the game continues with the qualified participants. When a pot is won, the house keeps 5% and the amulet moves counterclockwise.

Marked cards

Only a deck owner with an item slugged marked-playing-cards may use marked cards. On the first hand, they can select exactly two opening cards; on later hands, marked-card sight can reveal the concealed hands and discard pile. Whenever they cheat, they choose a blind Performance check or a blind Deception check using Create a Diversion. The result is compared privately with each observer’s Perception DC, and observers plus the GM receive a whisper only on a failure or critical failure against that observer.

Source acknowledgement. Golem originates in Pathfinder #159: All or Nothing, p. 76, as presented by Archives of Nethys.
